## Summary

What changes, why, and any related issue:

## Validation

List the checks actually run and their results. For extensions, include AiderDesk version, OS, installation scope, exercised behavior, and reload/unload testing. Explain anything not tested. For documentation-only changes, describe link/content checks; runtime checks can be marked not applicable.

## Trust and compatibility impact

For extension changes: dependencies/install scripts, external services, credentials, data access/transmission, changed permissions expectations, breaking changes, and migration steps. Use "not applicable" for documentation-only work.

## Checklist

Mark non-applicable items explicitly rather than implying they were tested.

- [ ] Changes are focused and follow CONTRIBUTING.md.
- [ ] Documentation and relative links are accurate; catalog updated if an extension is added or changed.
- [ ] Extension entry point, stable ID, static metadata, and required runtime files follow the supported layout (or not applicable).
- [ ] Relevant tests/type checks/builds and manual AiderDesk checks are described above (or not applicable).
- [ ] Dependencies, lifecycle scripts, external services, credential handling, and privacy implications are documented (or not applicable).
- [ ] No secrets, personal data, or sensitive project content appear in code, logs, fixtures, or screenshots.
- [ ] Licensing and attribution are preserved; any proposed exception to MIT is explicitly identified for approval.

Contributions are submitted under the repository's MIT license unless an explicitly documented and approved exception applies. Acceptance is not a security guarantee. Do not disclose vulnerabilities here; follow SECURITY.md.
